prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map separates the near foreground—the camera wearer’s yellow torso and nearby people’s legs/hands, roughly 0.2–1 m away—from the grass and standing people/dogs farther ahead, roughly 1–4 m away; the upper background is darkest and therefore farthest. Across the five frames, a person initially near the lower-right remains close while the wearer turns right, bringing another person’s legs and hand into the near-right foreground and shifting more distant people and dogs laterally across the view. Bright overlapping regions reveal that foreground bodies occlude the ground and more distant figures, with several people, limbs, and dogs partly cut off at the top or side boundaries. This map makes near/far layering and surface continuity clearer than RGB, but its absolute metre estimates are uncertain, boundaries bleed around bodies, and the nearly black upper field loses distinctions among distant grass, people, and dogs.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map identifies multiple people around the wearer, at least two dogs, a small sports ball near the left side in the first frame, and a cell phone near the center-right in the fourth frame, while separating overlapping foreground bodies into instances. The large person masks along the bottom and right correspond to people within roughly 0.3–1.5 m, whereas the small upper-edge people and dogs are roughly 2–5 m away; relative spacing is visible from the gaps and overlaps between masks, though the map itself does not encode metric distance. Across the sequence, people shift from the right toward the center as the camera turns, a large nearby person increasingly occupies the center-right, and other figures or limbs enter and leave through the top and side edges; mask overlap shows who is in front of whom but not reliably which way they face or whether they look toward the wearer. This map exposes small objects and occlusion ownership that are easy to miss in RGB, but it fragments some people, mislabels or merges adjacent regions, omits much of the scene, and gives unstable masks for the dogs, ball, phone, and partly visible limbs.
descriptions.pose: The pose map detects one main yellow body skeleton in the middle frames, about 1–2 m in front of the wearer and low in the image, plus a small magenta hand region farther right; nearly all other visible people and hands receive no usable pose. The yellow joints indicate a crouched or bent body with limbs extending laterally, but heavy overlap, foreshortening, and missing head landmarks make facing direction and gaze toward the wearer indeterminate. From frame three to four the detected body shifts slightly right and changes joint configuration as either the person or camera turns, while the hand appears separately to the right; frames one, two, and five contain no reliable skeleton for tracking approach or retreat. Pose could make articulated limb positions and potential reach clearer than RGB—the detected limbs appear within roughly an arm’s length of that person’s torso—but here it is highly unreliable because joints connect implausibly, hands are detached, occluded limbs disappear, and most nearby bodies are missed.
